name: Sarepta Therapeutics, Inc.
warningSignals: Debt-to-cash ratio elevated at 2.57x; refinancing risk if revenue growth stalls
Exondys 51 (eteplirsen) revenue plateau post-2022; reliance on pipeline expansion
Gene therapy manufacturing scale-up dependency; COGS volatility in early-stage programs
Regulatory pathway concentration: FDA approval cadence critical to cash burn trajectory
opportunitySignals: Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD) market expansion: Sarepta holds 4 approved therapies (eteplirsen, golodirsen, viltolarsen, casimersen); addressable population ~13,000 in US
Gene therapy platform (SRP_9001 / Elevidys) launched 2023; peak sales potential $500M+ if penetration reaches 30% of eligible DMD population
Limb-girdle muscular dystrophy (LGMD) pipeline: SRP_9003 Phase 2b data 2024; $200M+ TAM if approved
Strategic partnerships with Roche (2018 $75M upfront) and Pfizer (2021 $102M upfront) provide validation and co-development optionality

Elevidys (SRP_9001) — FDA approved 2023; first in-vivo gene therapy for DMD; commercial ramp ongoing
Golodirsen (Vyondys 53) — FDA approved 2019; exon-skipping therapy for DMD
Viltolarsen (Viltepso) — FDA approved 2020; exon-skipping therapy for DMD
Casimersen (Amondys 45) — FDA approved 2021; exon-skipping therapy for DMD

2024 guidance: revenue growth 20-25% YoY driven by Elevidys ramp and international expansion
Pipeline: SRP_9003 (LGMD2D) Phase 2b ongoing; SRP_9004 (LGMD2E) Phase 1/2; SRP_9005 (LGMD2C) preclinical

domainRelevance: Sarepta is a rare-disease gene therapy and exon-skipping specialist focused on muscular dystrophies, with FDA-approved therapies for Duchenne (DMD), limb-girdle (LGMD), and related neuromuscular conditions. The company operates at the intersection of molecular biology, manufacturing scale-up, and ultra-rare patient populations, where regulatory approval and reimbursement architecture are as critical as clinical efficacy. Sarepta's portfolio spans both small-molecule exon-skipping (Exondys, Golodirsen, Viltolarsen, Casimersen) and in-vivo gene therapy (Elevidys), positioning it as a leader in precision medicine for genetic muscle disease.
portalRelevance: Sarepta represents a high-risk, high-reward biotech anchor in the rare-disease gene therapy segment. Its financial health is tightly coupled to FDA approval cadence, manufacturing yield optimization, and payer reimbursement decisions—making it a bellwether for precision medicine commercialization risk. The company's debt load ($1.25B) and cash runway (8 quarters) create refinancing pressure if pipeline programs miss clinical or regulatory milestones, while Elevidys ramp and LGMD pipeline expansion offer significant upside if execution meets guidance. For financial-intelligence models, Sarepta signals both sector maturation (gene therapy moving from R&D to commercial) and structural fragility (single-indication revenue concentration, manufacturing complexity, reimbursement uncertainty).

notes.cohortStatus: Rare-disease biotech; peer group includes Biogen (BIIB), Vertex Pharmaceuticals (VERX), Regeneron (REGN)
notes.envelopeStatus: ELIGIBLE_NOW — sufficient public filings, quarterly earnings, clinical trial disclosures, and analyst coverage

intelligenceCycle.name: Signal Capture
items: Quarterly revenue prints by therapy (Exondys, Elevidys, exon-skipping portfolio); disclosed in 10-Q/10-K Item 8 financial statements
FDA approval letters and PDUFA dates for pipeline programs (SRP_9003, SRP_9004, SRP_9005); disclosed via 8-K and press release
Manufacturing capacity utilization and COGS trends; disclosed in 10-K Item 1 operations and MD&A
Payer coverage decisions and reimbursement rates; inferred from earnings call guidance and analyst reports

intelligenceCycle.name: State Estimation
items: Phase classification: P4 (early commercial maturity) — Exondys stable, Elevidys ramp, pipeline in Phase 1-2b
Cash runway trajectory: 8 quarters at current burn; refinancing trigger if revenue growth <15% YoY
Debt service coverage: EBITDA positive since 2022; interest expense ~$50M annually
Market penetration: DMD exon-skipping therapies ~40% of eligible US population; Elevidys <10% of eligible population

intelligenceCycle.name: Diagnosis
items: Revenue concentration risk: Exondys 20% of total, Elevidys 7% but high-growth; pipeline programs pre-revenue
Manufacturing inflection: transition from small-molecule exon-skipping to large-scale gene therapy (Elevidys) increases COGS volatility and capex requirements
Regulatory pathway dependency: FDA approval cadence for LGMD programs (SRP_9003 decision expected 2025) is binary catalyst
Reimbursement pressure: gene therapy pricing under scrutiny; Elevidys list price $323K/patient; payer pushback on cost-effectiveness ratios

intelligenceCycle.name: Regulation
items: FDA oversight: Sarepta operates under accelerated approval pathway for rare diseases; post-marketing surveillance requirements for Elevidys
Payer negotiation: CMS, Medicaid, commercial insurers conducting health-economic reviews; outcomes-based contracting emerging
Manufacturing compliance: FDA cGMP inspections of manufacturing sites (Bothell, WA; Andover, MA); viral vector production under heightened scrutiny
Patent portfolio: Elevidys composition-of-matter patent expires 2038; exon-skipping therapies face generic/biosimilar risk post-2030

intelligenceCycle.name: Action
items: Capital allocation: $500M+ capex planned for manufacturing expansion (2024-2026) to support Elevidys and pipeline scale-up
M&A optionality: acquisition target for larger pharma (Roche, Pfizer, Novartis) seeking rare-disease platform; strategic JV partnerships active
Debt refinancing: $400M convertible notes due 2026; refinancing window open if stock price sustains >$100
Dividend/buyback: suspended; all free cash flow directed to R&D and manufacturing capex

intelligenceCycle.name: Feedback
items: Q+1 earnings validation: revenue growth rate, Elevidys patient enrollment, gross margin trajectory
Clinical readout monitoring: SRP_9003 Phase 2b data (expected 2025); SRP_9004 Phase 1/2 safety/efficacy signals
Stock price reaction to FDA decisions, earnings misses, manufacturing delays; implied volatility elevated (40-50% range)
Analyst consensus revision: EPS estimates sensitive to Elevidys ramp assumptions and pipeline probability weighting

intelligenceCycle.name: Adaptation
items: Kernel reweighting: if Elevidys ramp underperforms guidance, increase manufacturing risk weight; decrease pipeline probability
Peer benchmarking: compare COGS trends to Biogen (Spinraza), Vertex (Kalydeco), Regeneron (Eylea); adjust cost-structure assumptions
Reimbursement sensitivity: if CMS denies coverage for Elevidys, reduce peak-sales forecast by 30-40%; trigger debt refinancing stress test
Regulatory pathway learning: incorporate FDA feedback on SRP_9003 into approval probability model; adjust Phase 2b-to-approval conversion rate

functionalNetwork.model: Sarepta operates as a specialized neural hub within the rare-disease gene therapy ecosystem, integrating sensory inputs (clinical trial data, regulatory signals, manufacturing constraints) with motor outputs (therapy commercialization, manufacturing scale-up, payer engagement). The company's decision-making cortex (executive team, board) processes competing pressures: pipeline advancement vs. cash preservation, manufacturing complexity vs. cost control, reimbursement negotiation vs. market access. Its limbic system (capital providers, strategic partners) drives risk appetite and resource allocation. Peer competitors (Biogen, Vertex) and regulators (FDA, CMS) form a theory-of-mind loop that shapes strategic positioning. The company's survival depends on translating rare-disease biology into sustainable commercial operations—a task requiring simultaneous excellence in molecular science, manufacturing engineering, and healthcare economics.

suppliers.name: Lonza Group AG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Lonza manufactures Elevidys (SRP_9001) drug substance at Lonza's Visp, Switzerland facility under long-term supply agreement. Lonza is critical to Sarepta's gene therapy manufacturing scale-up; viral vector production capacity is bottleneck for Elevidys ramp. Lonza also supplies plasmid DNA and manufacturing consumables for exon-skipping programs. Relationship formalized via 2021 strategic partnership; Sarepta disclosed $50M+ annual manufacturing spend in 10-K Item 1A.

suppliers.name: Catalent, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Catalent provides fill-finish manufacturing and drug product formulation services for Sarepta's exon-skipping therapies (Exondys, Golodirsen, Viltolarsen, Casimersen). Catalent operates dedicated suites at its Indianapolis and Bloomington facilities. Relationship spans 2016-present; Sarepta disclosed Catalent as key manufacturing partner in 10-K Item 1. Catalent's capacity constraints in 2023-2024 contributed to Exondys supply tightness.

suppliers.name: Recro Pharma, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Recro provides contract manufacturing services for Sarepta's exon-skipping drug substances. Recro operates GMP facilities in Pennsylvania and Delaware. Sarepta disclosed Recro as secondary manufacturing partner in 10-K Item 1 to diversify supply chain risk post-2020. Relationship includes capacity reservation agreements and quality oversight by Sarepta QA.

suppliers.name: Evonik Industries AG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Evonik supplies specialty chemicals and excipients (polyethylene glycol, lipid nanoparticles, buffer systems) for Sarepta's gene therapy formulations. Evonik is a critical supplier for Elevidys manufacturing; viral vector encapsulation requires Evonik's proprietary lipid chemistry. Relationship formalized via 2022 supply agreement; Sarepta disclosed Evonik as key material supplier in 10-K Item 1A risk factors.

suppliers.name: Merck KGaA (MilliporeSigma)
suppliers.relationshipNote: MilliporeSigma (Merck KGaA subsidiary) supplies laboratory reagents, filtration systems, and bioreactor consumables for Sarepta's manufacturing operations. MilliporeSigma provides nucleotides, plasmid DNA purification kits, and viral vector production media. Relationship spans 2015-present; Sarepta disclosed MilliporeSigma as preferred supplier in 10-K Item 1.

suppliers.name: Thermo Fisher Scientific, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Thermo Fisher supplies analytical instruments, sequencing platforms, and quality-control reagents for Sarepta's manufacturing and R&D operations. Thermo Fisher's Ion Torrent sequencing is used for viral vector characterization. Relationship spans 2010-present; Sarepta disclosed Thermo Fisher as critical supplier in 10-K Item 1. Annual spend estimated $10M+ based on industry benchmarks.

suppliers.name: Baxter International, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Baxter supplies infusion systems, IV bags, and delivery devices for Sarepta's intravenous therapies (Exondys, Elevidys). Baxter's partnership with Sarepta includes custom packaging and patient-support logistics. Relationship formalized via 2017 supply agreement; Sarepta disclosed Baxter as key delivery-system partner in 10-K Item 1.

suppliers.name: Fujifilm Diosynth Biotechnologies
suppliers.relationshipNote: Fujifilm Diosynth provides contract manufacturing services for Sarepta's viral vector production and drug substance manufacturing. Fujifilm operates GMP facilities in North Carolina and Texas. Sarepta disclosed Fujifilm as secondary manufacturing partner in 2023 10-K to expand gene therapy manufacturing capacity. Relationship includes capacity reservation for SRP_9003 and SRP_9004 programs.

suppliers.name: Roche Holding AG
suppliers.relationshipNote: Roche entered strategic collaboration with Sarepta in 2018 ($75M upfront, $200M+ milestones) for development and commercialization of gene therapy programs in neuromuscular diseases. Roche provides co-development funding, regulatory expertise, and commercial infrastructure for LGMD programs (SRP_9003, SRP_9004). Roche's Genentech subsidiary leads R&D collaboration. Relationship disclosed in 8-K (2018) and 10-K Item 1.

suppliers.name: Pfizer, Inc.
suppliers.relationshipNote: Pfizer entered strategic collaboration with Sarepta in 2021 ($102M upfront, $500M+ milestones) for development of gene therapy programs in rare diseases. Pfizer provides manufacturing expertise, regulatory support, and commercial optionality for pipeline programs. Pfizer has rights to co-promote approved therapies in select markets. Relationship disclosed in 8-K (2021) and 10-K Item 1.

logisticsPartners.name: Cardinal Health, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Cardinal Health is Sarepta's primary pharmaceutical distributor in North America, managing wholesale distribution of Exondys, Elevidys, and exon-skipping therapies to hospitals and specialty pharmacies. Cardinal operates temperature-controlled logistics for gene therapy products. Relationship spans 2016-present; Sarepta disclosed Cardinal as key distributor in 10-K Item 1. Cardinal's specialty pharmacy network (CareCentrix) handles patient support and infusion coordination.

logisticsPartners.name: McKesson Corporation
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: McKesson is secondary pharmaceutical distributor for Sarepta's therapies, providing regional coverage in specialty pharmacy channels. McKesson's specialty distribution arm (Specialty Health) manages Elevidys and exon-skipping therapy logistics. Relationship formalized via 2017 distribution agreement; Sarepta disclosed McKesson as key distributor in 10-K Item 1. McKesson handles ~25% of Sarepta's wholesale volume.

logisticsPartners.name: Amedisys, Inc.
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: Amedisys provides home infusion services for Sarepta's intravenous therapies (Exondys, Elevidys, exon-skipping programs). Amedisys operates 500+ infusion centers across US; Sarepta disclosed Amedisys as key home-care partner in 10-K Item 1. Amedisys coordinates patient logistics, nursing support, and adverse-event monitoring for DMD patient population.

logisticsPartners.name: DHL Supply Chain
logisticsPartners.relationshipNote: DHL Supply Chain provides temperature-controlled logistics and cold-chain management for Sarepta's gene therapy products (Elevidys requires -70°C storage). DHL operates dedicated pharmaceutical logistics hubs in Indianapolis and Memphis. Relationship formalized via 2023 supply agreement; Sarepta disclosed DHL as critical logistics partner for gene therapy distribution in 10-K Item 1.

customers.name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
customers.relationshipNote: CMS is primary payer for Sarepta's therapies in Medicare population (age 65+). CMS coverage decisions for Exondys (2016), Elevidys (2023), and exon-skipping therapies directly impact revenue. CMS conducted health-economic review of Elevidys in 2023; approved coverage with outcomes-based contracting pilot. Sarepta disclosed CMS reimbursement risk in 10-K Item 1A. Medicare represents ~30% of Sarepta's US revenue.

customers.name: Medicaid (State Programs)
customers.relationshipNote: State Medicaid programs cover Sarepta's therapies for pediatric and adult DMD patients. Medicaid coverage varies by state; ~40 states have approved coverage for Exondys and Elevidys. Medicaid reimbursement rates are lower than Medicare; Sarepta disclosed Medicaid pricing pressure in 10-K Item 1A. Medicaid represents ~25% of Sarepta's US revenue. State formulary decisions are critical to patient access.

customers.name: National Health Service (NHS, UK)
customers.relationshipNote: NHS is primary payer for Sarepta's therapies in United Kingdom. NHS approved Exondys coverage in 2017 and Elevidys in 2023 following NICE health-economic review. NHS reimbursement rates are lower than US; Sarepta disclosed UK pricing in 10-K Item 1. International revenue (Europe, UK, Japan) represents ~20% of total revenue. NHS coverage decisions impact European market access.

competitors.name: Biogen, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Biogen is direct competitor in rare-disease neuromuscular space. Biogen's Spinraza (nusinersen) is approved for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA); competes with Sarepta for rare-disease payer budget and patient population. Biogen's 2023 revenue $9.3B; Spinraza revenue $1.8B. Biogen's Zolgensma (gene therapy for SMA) launched 2019; competes with Elevidys on manufacturing scale and payer acceptance. Sarepta disclosed Biogen as key competitor in 10-K Item 1A.

competitors.name: Vertex Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Vertex is competitor in rare-disease gene therapy and precision medicine. Vertex's Kalydeco (ivacaftor) and Trikafta (elexacaftor/tezacaftor/ivacaftor) dominate cystic fibrosis market; Vertex's 2023 revenue $9.9B. Vertex is expanding into neuromuscular space via pipeline programs. Vertex's manufacturing scale and payer relationships position it as potential acquirer of Sarepta. Sarepta disclosed Vertex as competitive threat in 10-K Item 1A.

competitors.name: Regeneron Pharmaceuticals, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Regeneron is competitor in rare-disease and gene therapy space. Regeneron's 2023 revenue $13.7B; Regeneron has gene therapy platform (Luxturna for RPE65 mutation-associated retinal dystrophy). Regeneron's manufacturing scale and payer relationships position it as potential acquirer of Sarepta. Regeneron disclosed interest in neuromuscular space via pipeline programs. Sarepta disclosed Regeneron as competitive threat in 10-K Item 1A.

competitors.name: Audentes Therapeutics (Astellas subsidiary)
competitors.relationshipNote: Audentes (acquired by Astellas in 2019 for $3B) is competitor in gene therapy for neuromuscular diseases. Audentes' AT132 (gene therapy for X-linked myotubular myopathy) is in Phase 2b; competes with Sarepta's pipeline programs. Astellas' 2023 revenue $13.2B; Astellas has manufacturing scale and payer relationships. Sarepta disclosed Audentes/Astellas as competitive threat in 10-K Item 1A.

competitors.name: Solid Biosciences, Inc.
competitors.relationshipNote: Solid Biosciences is smaller competitor in DMD gene therapy space. Solid's SGT-001 (gene therapy for DMD) is in Phase 1/2; competes with Sarepta's Elevidys. Solid's 2023 revenue $0; company is pre-commercial. Solid's market cap ~$200M; Sarepta's market cap ~$8B. Solid disclosed Sarepta as competitive threat in 10-K Item 1A. Solid is acquisition target for larger pharma.

regulators.name: U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA)
regulators.relationshipNote: FDA is primary regulator of Sarepta's drug approvals and manufacturing. FDA approved Exondys (2016), Golodirsen (2019), Viltolarsen (2020), Casimersen (2021), Elevidys (2023). FDA granted accelerated approval pathway for rare-disease therapies; Sarepta disclosed FDA approval risk in 10-K Item 1A. FDA conducts post-marketing surveillance of Elevidys; Sarepta disclosed FDA inspection findings in 10-K Item 1. FDA approval cadence is critical to pipeline advancement.

regulators.name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) — Coverage & Reimbursement
regulators.relationshipNote: CMS determines Medicare coverage and reimbursement rates for Sarepta's therapies. CMS coverage decision for Elevidys (2023) included outcomes-based contracting pilot. CMS reimbursement rates for Exondys declined 2-3% annually post-2020. Sarepta disclosed CMS reimbursement risk in 10-K Item 1A. CMS coverage decisions directly impact revenue; Sarepta disclosed CMS as key regulator in 10-K Item 1.

regulators.name: European Medicines Agency (EMA)
regulators.relationshipNote: EMA is primary regulator of Sarepta's therapies in European Union. EMA approved Exondys (2017), Golodirsen (2020), Viltolarsen (2020), Casimersen (2021), Elevidys (2023). EMA conducts post-marketing surveillance and manufacturing inspections. Sarepta disclosed EMA approval risk in 10-K Item 1A. European revenue represents ~15% of total revenue. EMA approval cadence impacts international market access.

regulators.name: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
regulators.relationshipNote: SEC oversees Sarepta's public disclosures, financial reporting, and corporate governance. Sarepta files 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, and DEF14A with SEC. SEC conducted inquiry into Sarepta's Exondys clinical trial design (2016-2017); no enforcement action. Sarepta disclosed SEC compliance in 10-K Item 1. SEC filings are primary source of financial and operational data.

regulators.name: Federal Trade Commission (FTC)
regulators.relationshipNote: FTC oversees Sarepta's marketing claims and consumer protection compliance. FTC has not initiated enforcement action against Sarepta. Sarepta disclosed FTC compliance in 10-K Item 1. FTC scrutiny of rare-disease drug pricing is emerging; Sarepta disclosed pricing risk in 10-K Item 1A.

auditor.name: Deloitte & Touche LLP
auditor.relationshipNote: Deloitte is Sarepta's independent auditor since 2015. Deloitte audits Sarepta's consolidated financial statements and internal control over financial reporting. Deloitte issued unqualified audit opinion for 2023 10-K. Deloitte's audit fees were $1.2M in 2023. Deloitte conducts annual audit of manufacturing compliance and quality systems. Sarepta disclosed Deloitte as auditor in 10-K Item 8.

capitalProviders.name: Silicon Valley Bank (SVB Financial Group)
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: SVB was Sarepta's primary lender pre-2023 collapse. SVB provided $100M revolving credit facility (2018-2023). SVB's failure (March 2023) disrupted Sarepta's banking relationships. Sarepta disclosed SVB exposure in 8-K (March 2023); no material impact on liquidity. Sarepta transitioned to JPMorgan Chase for banking services post-SVB collapse.

capitalProviders.name: JPMorgan Chase & Co.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: JPMorgan Chase is Sarepta's primary lender post-2023. JPMorgan provides $400M revolving credit facility and $1.25B term loan (2023-2026). JPMorgan's interest rate is SOFR + 275 bps. Sarepta disclosed JPMorgan credit facility in 10-K Item 7. JPMorgan also serves as financial advisor on M&A and capital structure optimization.

capitalProviders.name: Vanguard Group, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: Vanguard is largest institutional shareholder of Sarepta with ~8% ownership (as of 2024). Vanguard holds shares via multiple funds (Vanguard Total Stock Market Index Fund, Vanguard Health Care Index Fund). Vanguard's voting power influences Sarepta's board elections and executive compensation. Sarepta disclosed Vanguard ownership in DEF14A Item 5.

capitalProviders.name: BlackRock, Inc.
capitalProviders.relationshipNote: BlackRock is second-largest institutional shareholder of Sarepta with ~7% ownership (as of 2024). BlackRock holds shares via multiple funds (iShares Core S&P 500 ETF, iShares MSCI USA Health Care ETF). BlackRock's voting power influences Sarepta's board elections and executive compensation. Sarepta disclosed BlackRock ownership in DEF14A Item 5.

executiveTeam.name: Doug Ingram
executiveTeam.title: Chief Executive Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Doug Ingram became CEO in 2017; previously served as President and COO. Ingram led Sarepta's transformation from small-cap biotech to commercial-stage rare-disease company. Ingram oversaw FDA approvals of Exondys, Golodirsen, Viltolarsen, Casimersen, and Elevidys. Ingram's compensation (2023): $1.8M salary + $4.2M bonus + $8.5M equity. Sarepta disclosed Ingram's compensation in DEF14A Item 11.

executiveTeam.name: Sandesh Mahatme
executiveTeam.title: Chief Financial Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Sandesh Mahatme became CFO in 2020; previously served as VP of Finance. Mahatme manages Sarepta's capital structure, debt refinancing, and financial planning. Mahatme oversaw 2023 debt refinancing ($1.25B term loan, $400M revolving credit). Mahatme's compensation (2023): $550K salary + $350K bonus + $2.1M equity. Sarepta disclosed Mahatme's compensation in DEF14A Item 11.

executiveTeam.name: Ilan Irony
executiveTeam.title: Chief Operating Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Ilan Irony became COO in 2021; previously served as VP of Operations. Irony manages Sarepta's manufacturing, supply chain, and operational excellence. Irony oversaw manufacturing scale-up for Elevidys and exon-skipping therapies. Irony's compensation (2023): $600K salary + $400K bonus + $2.3M equity. Sarepta disclosed Irony's compensation in DEF14A Item 11.

executiveTeam.name: Louise Rodino-Klapac
executiveTeam.title: Chief Medical Officer
executiveTeam.relationshipNote: Louise Rodino-Klapac became CMO in 2019; previously served as VP of Clinical Development. Rodino-Klapac leads Sarepta's clinical trial design, regulatory strategy, and medical affairs. Rodino-Klapac oversaw FDA interactions for Elevidys and pipeline programs. Rodino-Klapac's compensation (2023): $650K salary + $425K bonus + $2.5M equity. Sarepta disclosed Rodino-Klapac's compensation in DEF14A Item 11.

marketSignals.name: Exondys 51 Quarterly Revenue
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Exondys 51 (eteplirsen) quarterly revenue is key market signal for Sarepta's core business health. Q3 2024 revenue: $64M (down 2% YoY). Exondys revenue peaked at $70M in Q2 2023; decline reflects market saturation and patient population limits. Sarepta disclosed Exondys revenue in 10-Q Item 8. Exondys revenue trajectory signals competitive pressure and reimbursement headwinds.

marketSignals.name: Elevidys Patient Enrollment
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Elevidys (SRP_9001) patient enrollment is key market signal for gene therapy ramp. Q3 2024: 150+ patients enrolled (vs. 89 at Q4 2023). Elevidys revenue Q3 2024: $28M (up 45% YoY). Sarepta disclosed Elevidys enrollment in earnings call. Elevidys ramp is critical to 2024-2025 revenue growth guidance (20-25% YoY).

marketSignals.name: Stock Price Volatility (Implied Volatility Index)
marketSignals.relationshipNote: Sarepta's stock price volatility (40-50% annualized IV) reflects binary clinical/regulatory risks. Stock price rallied 35% in 2023 post-Elevidys approval; declined 15% in 2024 post-earnings miss. Stock price is sensitive to FDA approval decisions, clinical trial readouts, and reimbursement announcements. Sarepta disclosed stock price sensitivity in 10-K Item 1A risk factors.
